# Execution Feedback and Action Correction

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](execution-feedback_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Robot Manipulation Policies and Control → Execution Feedback and Action Correction

Execution monitoring, action correction and failure recovery as the main contribution. Specify whether feedback changes commands, subsequent observations or model parameters. Ordinary closed-loop input alone does not qualify.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.FEEDBACK.1] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-feedback-1"></a> | **FOMO-Dex｜Force-feedback compliance · Task-direction selection · Corrected-action imitation learning**<br>[Force-Modulated Dexterity: Unified Compliance for Contact-Rich Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17161v1)<br>Ying Yuan, David Held, Jitendra Malik, Haozhi Qi<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `execution-feedback` `action-correction` `force-feedback` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `compliant-control` `admittance-control` `task-frame-control` `direction-selective-compliance` `teleoperation` `demonstration-collection` `post-modulation-action-targets` `imitation-learning` `behavior-cloning` `diffusion-policy` `real-world` | FOMO-Dex selects compliant directions from task and contact geometry, converts robot force feedback into arm-pose or finger-joint corrections while preserving task motion, and trains a diffusion policy on the corrected commands so autonomous manipulation learns the force-dependent adjustments.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The controller projects wrist/fingertip force feedback onto configured directions, converts target/limit errors through admittance into command corrections, and does not learn compliance parameters online. Cutting preserves forward motion while relieving lateral/excess normal loading; rotational tasks regulate fingertip loads while retaining rotation. Hardware uses a 7-DoF Tianji Marvin arm and 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hand. Controller tests cover card picking, paper cutting, nut–bolt manipulation and screwdriving. Behavior cloning uses frozen DINOv2, RGB/proprioception/force observations and a diffusion policy with 50 demonstrations per task–controller setting. Across 18 card-picking trials, corrected-action training with stiff execution achieves 67% lift success, versus 0% for raw-command training with deployment-time compliance and 56% for stiff demonstrations. Rotational-policy results measure turns per episode, not success rates. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17161v1) · [Project](https://yingyuan0414.github.io/fomo-dex/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.VLA.FEEDBACK.1] <a id="am-man-dex-vla-feedback-1"></a> | **AgenticTactileVLA｜VLA · Contact feedback · Online action correction**<br>[AgenticTactileVLA: Contact-Guided Execution-Time Supervision for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation without VLA Retraining](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04391v1)<br>Elizaveta Semenyakina et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `execution-feedback` `action-correction` `proprioception` [contact-estimation](../../../topics/tactile.md) `compliant-control` `grasping` `pick-and-place` `real-world` | **Feedback/correction:** After nominal VLA finger closure, detect contact evidence from commanded-versus-measured finger motion and, during correction, motor-effort feedback. If support is insufficient, pause body-reference progression while maintaining stabilization and advance unsupported fingers independently until contact. Retain the corrected hand configuration when support criteria pass; otherwise return control to the VLA for retry.<br>**Where it acts:** An external, nonlearned supervisor changes executed commands; the corrected hand state enters subsequent VLA observations without updating VLA parameters. The base VLA was fine-tuned on teleoperated demonstrations.<br>**Compliant mode:** Before closure, language cues or a VLM select predefined current-limited control for fragile objects. No additional tactile sensors are required; motor feedback is not calibrated contact force.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Unitree G1 with BrainCo Revo2 and fixed GR00T-N1.6-3B; five held-out objects, 15 matched trials per object, with a shared 60-second/three-approach budget. Completion rises from 61.3% for the base VLA to 84.0% (72.0% for unconditional close-to-stall). The compliant branch evaluates object integrity during closure and holding, not autonomous transport; cross-hand and cross-VLA generality are not established. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04391v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-22 |
